currentUse: Exploratory recognition of string themes; not a representative social trend.
unit: One distinct primary string per comparison cohort; do not weight by application count unless a separate analysis explicitly does so.

codebook.rule: Use explicit lexical evidence and cited contextual documents; record ambiguity, polysemy and absence of evidence. Never infer applicant activity from this label.

sampling.selection: SHA-256 order of ctd-validation-v1|cohort|ascii_string, with available strata and deterministic fill. Purposive validation sample, not representative prevalence estimate.
sampling.language: Reviewers identify language/script; automatic inference of language from the suffix is not accepted.

reviewSteps: Two reviewers independently read each string with the same permitted context and codebook; hide the current machine label during first coding.
Allow zero, one or several themes. Use not-classified when evidence is insufficient; it is not a category of activity. Record source and reason.
Publish independent labels, ambiguity and agreement per category before adjudication. Report raw agreement and appropriate multi-label chance-corrected measures with sample limitations.
Adjudicate disagreements with sources, publish correction/error analysis and rules changed, then apply the same revised rules to both rounds.
Only after validation assess whether coverage and language bias permit stronger longitudinal claims; actual social use needs additional independent evidence.

operationalRules.inheritedThemePolicy: Source string-theme assertions are retained with their original evidence. They are never reused as an applicant sector. Round-specific official flags stay separate.
operationalRules.boundaryRule: Classify only the theme supported by the label and allowed source context; document polysemy, unsupported inference and language uncertainty. Multiple labels are allowed; category totals are not additive.
